body:
The `renderFn` function is mistyped, we shouldn't have to cast the connector params. Ideally we should be able to do:

```js
  return makeHitsPerPage<HitsPerPageWidgetOptions>({ items, transformItems });
```

`HitsPerPageWidgetOptions` can then be used to type `widgetParams` in the connector and renderer.

```suggestion
   * @default 'No results'
```

body: Should we default `THitsWidgetParams` to `any` here? Right now, users _have to_ specify a type when using the widget params.

We should be able to remove the `@ts-ignore`, cast and `__escaped` by using:

```ts
const expectedHits = escapeHits([ /* ... */ ]);
```
We can add `objectID`s to remove the need for `@ts-ignore`.
If relevant, we can cast as `EscapedHits`.
@francoischalifour My transformer function intentionally removes the objectID from the expected hits.

The test here is asserting that we proper escape hits behind the scenes, so the `expectedHits` contains escaped content already. I am doing a ts ignore because i don't know how to assign an array with a property in javascript. You do?

We are **defaulting to empty generic**, so they are not forced.

if they don't pass a generic, the params will be {} & connectorParams.
it says `= {}`, no?

I meant, if you want to access a widget param (e.g. `container`), you need to specify the `connectHits` type:

https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/62afb953f1bd34b53727eb6f2c6e37ae26e72596/stories/configure-related-items.stories.ts#L71-L83

Wondering if we should be less strict about it by defaulting to `any`?
@francoischalifour I don't think is a good idea. The goal of using TypeScript is provide type safety.  Defaulting to any, is defaulting to non safe code.
@Haroenv If you do `connectHits(` without generic, means that you don't have any widget params, besides the default connector params ones.
Makes sense!
